messages:
Harper: my downstairs neighbor renamed their SSID to 'NOT A TROJAN' and now my calls drop. anyone else dealing with hostile wifi branding? :rolling_eyes:
Diego: hah. channel overlap more likely. try a Wi-Fi analyzer app to see strong APs on your channel. Android: WiFi Analyzer, mac: Wireless Diagnostics.
Nina: poll time: most obnoxious SSID you've seen? 1) PrettyFlyForAWiFi 2) DropItLikeItsHotspot 3) FBI_Van_12 4) password123. react 1/2/3/4.
Jules: 1 for me. also saw "GetOffMyLawn" once. :older_man:
Marta: 3 sadly. scared my delivery driver last week.
Diego: practical fix: move to 5GHz if your devices support it, or set router to least congested channel. On Linux you can `sudo iwlist scan` to inspect.
Harper: any quick command for macOS to see channels?
Diego: on mac hold option and click Wi-Fi icon -> Open Wireless Diagnostics -> Window -> Scan. shows recommended channel.
Nina: security reminder: a funny SSID doesn't change whether you should use WPA2/3 and a strong passphrase. enable guest network for IoT.
StatusBot: Reminder: network maintenance in eu-central scheduled 01:00-01:30 UTC tomorrow. Some private endpoints may be briefly unreachable.
Harper: thanks @StatusBot. back to SSID names: we should make a generator. HarperBot: "Your router is watching you"? :laughing:
Jules: do it. I'll seed it with dad-joke combos.
Marta: also, if you have persistent drops, try toggling the router's coexistence/Bluetooth coexistence setting. helped my apartment where neighbors had a million smart devices.
Diego: final tip: if someone really renamed their SSID to something suspicious (FBI etc.) don't connect. report odd behavior to your building or ISP.
Nina: results: 1=2, 2=0, 3=1, 4=0. PrettyFly wins.
Harper: changing my SSID to "PrettyFly_Reverse" now. will test channel change and report back.
Jules: bonus: share SSID name if you win the internal contest. prize: eternal ridicule. :trophy:
Harper: will post before/after latency numbers later. cheers!
